notes:
Added a new Chromebook fleet → Assigned users tab that does both: blank the Assigned user field, or set it to the person who last signed in. All 277 tests pass. I ran the tab against my stand-in GAM, not your domain. That stand-in doesn’t report who last signed in, so the “set to last user” part has only been tested with sample data.

How it works
Pick which Chromebooks: all of them, one or more org units, a list of serials, or a list of asset IDs. Click Load.
Look at the table. Each device shows its current assigned user, who last signed in, a Plan (Set, Same or Skip) and a Why.
Set assigned users copies the last signed-in user into the field. Blank the assigned user… empties it. If you select rows, only those are changed; otherwise every loaded device is.
Undo last change puts the old values back. They’re saved to a CSV before any change, and Open backups shows those files.

These changes go through your usual approvals, dry run and role checks. Blanking the field doesn’t remove anyone’s profile or wipe the device.

Filters for the technician/teacher problem the other AI warned about

Only where it’s blank is on by default. Switch to Also replace a different user to overwrite, and GAMbit asks for an extra confirmation first.
Only students: the last user must be in a student org unit (the ones set on Student lookup).
Ignore list: for example tech*, helpdesk@.
Last used within N days skips old sign-ins.
Devices with no recent signed-in user, or whose last user is outside the district (like a Gmail account), are always skipped.
